Name: PENABLE
Structural Path: PENABLE -> APB access qualification -> PADDIR/GPIOLOCK write enable -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on PENABLE during a legal APB transfer changes whether or what value is written to gpio_dir.
Justification: A protocol-phase fault converts or suppresses the access cycle that updates the direction register.

Name: r_gpio_lock
Structural Path: r_gpio_lock -> PADDIR write authorization -> r_gpio_dir -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on r_gpio_lock during a legal APB transfer changes whether or what value is written to gpio_dir.
Justification: A one-bit lock fault removes write protection and was highly feasible with essentially no masking.

Name: PWDATA
Structural Path: PWDATA -> write-data path -> r_gpio_dir update -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on PWDATA during a legal APB transfer changes whether or what value is written to gpio_dir.
Justification: A data-line fault directly corrupts the value captured into the direction state.

Name: pwdata_l
Structural Path: pwdata_l -> latched APB write data -> r_gpio_dir update -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on pwdata_l during a legal APB transfer changes whether or what value is written to gpio_dir.
Justification: The latched write-data state is a distinct storage point whose corruption is consumed by the register update.

Name: PADDR
Structural Path: PADDR -> s_apb_addr -> register decode -> PADDIR write enable -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on PADDR during a legal APB transfer changes whether or what value is written to gpio_dir.
Justification: An address fault redirects a legal APB write into the direction-register decode.

Name: PSEL
Structural Path: PSEL -> APB transaction qualification -> PADDIR write enable -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on PSEL during a legal APB transfer changes whether or what value is written to gpio_dir.
Justification: A select fault creates or removes a qualifying peripheral transaction and changes the direction update.

Name: PWRITE
Structural Path: PWRITE -> read/write qualification -> PADDIR write enable -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on PWRITE during a legal APB transfer changes whether or what value is written to gpio_dir.
Justification: A read/write-control fault turns a non-writing access into a direction-register write.
